Bamboo Pearl over Light Gray leather, all-wheel drive, and 98,960 miles on a vehicle that turns seventeen this year. Two keys come with it.VIN: 2T2HK31U89C105884 | Odometer: 98,960 miles? What You're Actually Getting? Dealer Certified Pre-Owned  passed our 90-point inspection and meets our age, condition, and mileage criteria? All drive monitors completed, zero stored or pending trouble codes on our OBDII scan? 19 service history records and 39 detailed records on the CARFAX, running from the original 2008 pre-delivery inspection through this year  a documented vehicle, not a mystery? Complete front accessory belt drive replaced September 2025 at 98,798 miles  serpentine belt, drive belts, drive belt tensioner, serpentine tensioner, tensioner pulley, and idler pulley, with the battery and charging system checked at the same time. That's the entire belt-driven front end done at once, an estimated $950-$1,250 of durable failure-part work at dealer rates (estimate  CARFAX documents the work, not the invoice)? Real ValueHere's what the independent sources say about this vehicle, checked August 13, 2026: Kelley Blue Book typical dealer listing price: $8,175 Cars.com national average asking price, 2009 RX 350: $8,322 CARFAX History-Based Value: $11,310 retailThose don't line up, and we'd rather show you the disagreement than quietly pick the friendliest number. The honest read is a retail range of roughly $8,175 to $11,310. CARFAX sits at the top of that range because its model rewards exactly what this vehicle has  no accidents, a documented service history, and personal ownership throughout.For live context: actively listed second-generation RX 350s around metro Atlanta with 100,000 to 130,000 miles have been asking in the mid-to-high $9,000s, examples past 180,000 miles fall under $6,000, and the lowest-mileage cars at franchise Lexus stores reach into the low $13,000s. Our goal is that you never overpay and that you leave with as much value as we can put in your hands. Market pricing moves, so if you'd like a more current market pricing report on this vehicle, just ask and we'll pull one for you.?? Vehicle History (Full Transparency)The accident record is clean, and that's the easy part. CARFAX reports no accidents or damage, no structural damage, no airbag deployment, no total loss, and no odometer discrepancy  across all four owners and seventeen years. The title is CARFAX-guaranteed against salvage, junk, rebuilt, fire, flood, hail, and lemon branding.Four previous owners is more than average, so here's the actual shape of it. The first owner bought it new in Arizona in 2009 and kept it nearly five years, servicing it at Lexus dealers the whole time. It changed hands briefly in early 2014, then went to a Florida owner who kept it six and a half years and continued servicing it at a Lexus dealer and a national tire chain. The fourth owner held it six years in Naples. Every one of them was a personal owner, and every one of them drove it lightly. Four owners on a seventeen-year-old vehicle averages out to roughly four years each  that's ordinary, not a red flag.The low mileage comes with a real trade-off, and you should hear it from us. The most recent owner drove this vehicle about 651 miles a year  under 4,000 miles in six years. Low mileage is genuinely good for wear on the engine, transmission, and drivetrain. But a vehicle that sits ages differently than one that runs: rubber, seals, and belts age on the calendar regardless of the odometer. That's almost certainly why the entire belt drive  belts, tensioners, and pulleys  was replaced in September 2025 at under 99,000 miles, which is early for that job on mileage alone. The work is done and documented. The same logic is why this vehicle has four new tires on it now. The set it arrived on was installed in August 2023 and had covered barely 675 miles  the tread was essentially unused, and on tread depth alone nobody would have questioned selling it that way. But tires age by date code, not by wear, and three-year-old rubber on a vehicle that sat is not the same as three-year-old rubber on a vehicle that ran. So they were replaced.Other things worth knowing: all original factory coverage  basic, drivetrain, corrosion, and roadside  expired years ago. This is a seventeen-year-old luxury SUV and you should expect age-appropriate cosmetic wear inside and out. One specific exception is worth naming, because anyone who has researched this generation of RX already knows to look for it: the dashboards on these are prone to cracking with age and sun exposure, and plenty of otherwise-good examples have a spidered dash top. This one's dash is in great condition. Go look at it first  we'd rather you check than take our word for it.?? It lists the major systems a used vehicle can develop problems in  engine, transmission, drivetrain, brakes, cooling, fuel, electrical, suspension and more  and almost nobody reads it. That gap between what people sign and what people expect is where disappointment comes from. A used vehicle is a used vehicle, and we'd rather set that expectation honestly than make a promise that can't hold.
